subject: Post-demo recap: Nebula Labs hosted usage stretch, peak TPS, and budget targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: Nebula hosted usage stretch, peak TPS, and budget targets

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the asks I promised to pull together: 

Summary of the call:
- Primary workload: user-facing coding assistant + scheduled batch analysis for classification.
- Expected steady-state production: roughly 4.5M–6M tokens / month once feature set is live.
- Occasional product releases / marketing pushes: short bursts where we see traffic spike ~8–10x the baseline for 1–3 hour windows.
- Peak TPS we measured on your staging traces: sustained ~450 p50, with observed spikes to ~1,000 QPS during load tests. For planning, you mentioned a conservative 95th/99th target of ~600–800 TPS for day-to-day peaks and up to ~1,100 TPS during release windows.

Pricing/commit ask we discussed:
- Nebula target for unit economics: $900–$1,300 per 1M tokens (goal is to stay under $1,200 if possible).
- You asked whether Hosted API can support the bursts without Dedicated immediately — short answer: yes, with proper concurrency controls, autoscale, and burst capacity bands; we recommended a small committed slab to reduce unit price.

Attachments I am including here for your review:
- Nebula_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf — outline of pilot scope and timeline (two-week canary + 8-week ramp).
- pricing_workbook-nebula.xlsx — rough slab math for 3 pricing bands (no-commit, small-commit, medium-commit) based on the volumes above.

Concrete next steps / asks:
1) Jordan / Priya: confirm which monthly commit band (if any) you prefer for the pilot: None / 5M token slab / 10M token slab.
2) Karthik: can you run the slab math and propose the two pricing options to present (conservative and aggressive)?
3) Marissa to share a short SOW + DocuSign if Nebula is comfortable with the pilot timeline.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-min follow-up tomorrow to land the commit band — otherwise we’ll wait for your confirmation via email.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
redwoodinference.com
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@nebulalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nebulalabs.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Nebula hosted usage stretch, peak TPS, and budget targets

Thanks Marissa — that was helpful. Quick responses inline: 

- Confirmed: steady-state expected ~5M tokens/mo after ramp (we’ll likely be toward the high end of your 4.5–6M estimate).
- Bursts: during beta launches we regularly see ~1,000–1,200 TPS for the 1–3 hour release window. The 600–800 TPS is a good day-to-day planning number, but assume we need to cover the 1,200 TPS tail for safety.
- Budget: our procurement target is to keep unit cost under $1,200/1M tokens for the pilot.

One operational question: what happens if we hit the burst ceiling on Hosted — do requests queue, fail, or degrade? We need to understand fallback behavior and SLAs for the pilot. Can you include that in the SOW?

We’re leaning toward the 5M token pilot slab to start; Priya and I will confirm by EOD tomorrow once we run this past finance.

Jordan
Head of Product — Nebula Labs
j.ellis@nebulalabs.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: Nebula hosted usage stretch, peak TPS, and budget targets

Karthik / Vanessa — forwarding Jordan’s reply. Key takeaways for pricing: they expect ~5M/mo baseline and need safety for 1,200 TPS occasional spikes. Procurement wants <$1,200/1M for the pilot.

Internal notes / proposed approach:
- Offer two pilot options:
  1) Small-commit pilot (5M/mo slab, 6-month term): $1,100 per 1M tokens for the slab; Hosted with burst capacity up to 1,500 TPS (auto-throttled beyond that with graceful 429s + retry guidance).
  2) No-commit short pilot (2-week canary + month of telemetry): $1,350 per 1M tokens, standard Hosted QoS, spikes handled via burst lanes but lower priority and potential 429s under extreme contention.

Operational / SLA notes for SOW to include:
- Burst behavior: we provide best-effort burst lanes; when constrained, Redwood will return 429s with Retry-After headers and an automatic routing fallback to a heat-limited model variant (lower token cost, slightly higher latency) if configured.
- Monitoring: will include per-route 99th latency, token breakdown, and per-minute TPS.
- Escalation: 24x7 support for pilot; escalation path to SRE and AE.

Vanessa — please prepare the pricing_workbook numbers for the 5M slab (show net and modeled $/1M after credits) and a short one-pager comparing the two options for Jordan to share with finance.

I’ll prep the SOW draft and DocuSign link once they confirm the slab.

—
Marissa
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@nebulalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nebulalabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Nebula hosted usage stretch, peak TPS, and budget targets

Marissa / team — thanks. Priya and I reviewed: finance is okay to start the pilot at the 5M slab assuming the $1,100/1M number you proposed. Two quick asks before signature: 
1) Add the burst behavior wording into the SOW (explicit mention of 429s + Retry-After and fallback to heat-limited variant).
2) Can you confirm maximum sustained TPS per minute we can expect on Hosted under the 5M slab before we have to move to Dedicated (ballpark number)?

If you can add that language and confirm the TPS ceiling, we’ll sign the SOW and route it to DocuSign today.

Jordan
